name: Shared cosine geometry for multimodal registration
label: PILOT/DEVELOPMENT
question: With local matching encoded directly in a shared descriptor geometry, do quadratic J and its exact empirical reference moments improve registration relative to matched objectives?

theory.T: normalized local descriptor dot product, bounded by one
theory.P: aligned descriptor pairs within each sampled scene/crop
theory.Q: product of empirical local marginals within the same scene/crop, including diagonal; then average scenes
theory.qualification: conditional within-scene dependence, not global marginal-product QMI
theory.J: EP T - EQ T - 0.5 EP T^2 - 0.5 EQ T^2
theory.exact_moments: EQ T=mu_u dot mu_v; EQ T^2=tr(Cu Cv), uncentered moments

controls.vcs_perm: ordinary within-scene permutation, unbiased for the full empirical product conditional on descriptors
controls.bce: same bounded cosine T, twice balanced BCE centered at zero, probability clip1e-6; same full reference pairs
controls.nce: symmetric within-scene cosine InfoNCE, tau=.07 preset, strong ranking control; different objective scale disclosed

recipe.encoder_init: same host encoders and seed, no free pairwise critic
recipe.optimizer: AdamW lr3e-4, original weight decay and gradient clip
recipe.batch: 16 scenes x 128 positions, crop160, original sampler
recipe.primary_readout: mean aligned cosine for every objective
recipe.cal_selection: original loose success, strict success, lower median error, earlier step; three candidates for every arm
recipe.dev: both COS and exact J at CAL-selected checkpoint, full existing DEV, no further selection

evidence: application gains in strict and loose success, retain failure tails
VCS exact versus sampled isolates reference estimation under same geometry
VCS exact versus BCE isolates objective at same bounded score and full Q
NCE and existing historical hosts benchmark task competitiveness
report every arm and seed, all attempts, GPU runtime and peak memory
